\section{Introduction}
The Kaymakli West settlement mound rises 4.2~m above the
surrounding plain and covers an area of 3.4 hectares at its base.
Surface collections in 2021 suggested a long prehistoric
occupation, and the 2025 season was designed to test the depth
and continuity of that sequence.

Eighteen trenches were opened across the mound, including two
deep soundings placed on the northern and southern slopes.
The deep sounding in Trench~12 reached sterile soil at 3.9~m
and yielded a charcoal sample from its lowest occupation layer.

The ceramic corpus from the season comprises 14,203 diagnostic
sherds, dominated by burnished wares with a minority of painted
vessels concentrated in the upper levels.
Preliminary typological work places the earliest secure
occupation between 6200 and 5800~BCE, pending the radiocarbon
programme now underway.

This interim report summarises the stratigraphic sequence, the
finds corpus, and the sampling strategy for the coming year.
